for_senior_author: Women and men on MDMA (cl_mdma_response_predictors against the approved cl_mdma_feelings): Studerus 2021 (10 Basel studies, 194 people) found no significant sex association after allowing for dose per kilogram; cl_mdma_feelings reports, from Vizeli and Liechti 2017 (nine of the same studies), higher bad-effect ratings in women after that adjustment. The patched claim now carries the authors' own note on this conflict. Editors' reading: the difference may come from the outcome (area under the effect curve in Studerus, peak ratings in Vizeli and Liechti) and from Studerus's correction across 500 tests. Decide whether cl_mdma_feelings should point to this answer, or the page should state the two results together.

Two music trials on the project's list have no cards: Greenway et al. 2024 (randomized trial of music with ketamine for depression, JAMA Netw Open, PMC10845001) and Strickland et al. 2021 (randomized comparison of music genres with psilocybin, PMC8033606). cl_ket_music now says the 2024 trial has not been read; both claims should be revisited once these are carded.

cl_xc_music now includes the panel's imprecise odds ratio for music and later thoughts or attempts of harm (2.67, 0.87 to 8.21, not significant), because the claim's question covers 'what follows'. Decide whether it belongs in a music answer. It is kept out of the plain lines.

sc_kaelen_2018 risk-of-bias note (exposure domain) says the raters 'agreed only moderately (average r 0.6)'. The analysis used the four-rater average (about 0.86 by Spearman-Brown, editors' calculation), and the authors call the agreement good. This is domain-note wording, so I left it for you; the claim no longer says 'only moderately'.
cl_ket_music keeps status 'single study' (one review; for ketamine alone, one controlled comparison). Another flag is arguable for a review of 14 mixed studies; this is your call.
